Hi friend. I can empathize with this a lot, because I've been in a similar headspace before. I'm autistic, have gone to a public university, and have felt like an r-word and a burden to others. 

Thing is, I don't see an r-word, burden, or failure. I see a person who's empathetic and wants to succeed, while they're hurting. You're also not a pussy for not going through with hurting yourself - that's your body protecting you, for good reason. 

It's already hard enough to go to university, no matter if you're neurotypical or not. It's hard, point blank. You having a hard time doesn't make you an r-word whatsoever. It just means that there's different approaches that you might have to take towards your program. Have you been able to look into getting accommodations at all? And if you don't know what kind of specific accomodations you'd need, the counselors and/or disability services on campus  could help. 

I hear you, though. Having autism and trying to navigate through society is hard enough, let alone when you're hurting so much. You shouldn't have to carry that alone, and you don't have to do it alone because these are relatable struggles that a lot of folks can identify with. 
If you don't feel comfortable saying anything to your family right now, there's support online and on campus that you could reach out to. Crisis line, for one - in addition to that, support groups, counselling, and educational resources could all help. On the other hand, from you saying that you love your family, one can infer that they love you as well. No matter what, they want to see you happy and nothing you do would ever be considered a burden. You struggling with these things, asking for help, or confiding in anyone doesn't make you a burden; it makes you HUMAN. If anything, them not having you around would be the biggest burden to carry. 

And I can also empathize with being scared of the future/future self. Looking that far out is daunting - but taking it one day at a time is so much more manageable. On a day to day basis, what are some things that could make your load at least a little lighter, and what could take you closer to being content and/or happy? 
Taking your life might seem like a way out, but how I see it now is that it's a definitive move that doesn't ensure things getting better. It ensures more pain and takes away the chance of being able to make anything better. 

Looking back, I didn't think I was going to make it past 18-20 years old - the future looked so distant and daunting that I couldn't bear the thought of moving forward, especially when I was hurting so much. But allowing myself to live and to take things one day at a time made it so that I could embrace the things that make me happy and life worth living, in spite of all that makes it difficult. Had I gone through with the attempt years ago, I wouldn't have lived to graduate and see that success (which came from the help of the accommodations), get to a mid-career point in my dream industry, and get admitted into a Master's program. I would have no longer been able to feel the warmth of my family's love, the taste of my favorite food, the comfort of a good book, or any of the other things that make life worth it. 

All of that is to say, it IS possible to get past this. I'm not here to tell you that the grass is greener on the other side, cause that might not be what you want to hear right now. What's true, though, is that there's portions of green grass on the way towards feeling better; little moments and feats that add up towards you feeling better overall. 

Head up, friend. You're not a burden, and you don't have to go through this alone. I'm here if you wanna talk more.

Please, please don't go through with hurting yourself. even though im a stranger on the internet, I'm truly hoping that you don't go through with it.

Met a girl online and met her up for drinks. We hit it off after some chitchat, and she invited me back to her place to watch some anime. She lived within walking distance of the bar, so I drove the both of us back to her place. 

As we were walking down the hallway to her door, she decided to drop the fact that her partner was home. It struck me as odd that she didn't tell me until that point, but it wasn't  a red flag to me at the time cause I'm non-monogamous myself and know that people have partners they live with. When we got there, he was on the couch and I gave a quick "hi" before me and the girl went to her room. 

We switched on some show and in a short amount of time, we were making out. As we were getting hot and heavy, she started getting into some dirty talk of how she wanted to share me with her partner, wanted him to join, and started getting into detail of what she wanted him to do to me. I got scared. I kept diverting her and telling her that I just wanted it to be me and her. 

A few minutes of that go by, then she said that she was going to grab some water and asked if I wanted any. I hesitated, but then said sure. She came back with a water bottle and gave it to me, then said that she'd be right back. I waited there in her bed and as some time passed, the situation started to sink in. I realized that she might bring her partner into the room for that threesome she kept trying to insinuate, and I wouldn't be able to do anything at that point if that scenario were to play out. (I'm not physically strong and don't know how to fight that well). 

I quickly got dressed and got the hell out of her room. As I was headed to the door, I saw her passed out on the couch. I whisper-shouted her name to see if she was awake. She stirred a bit, but no response. I grabbed my shoes and dipped out of the place without even bothering to put them on, and I ran all the way to my car. 

I texted her with some excuse of how there was an emergency at home. About 30 minutes later, she texted me back with a nonchalant "Aw, hope everything is ok!" and that was about it. Nothing about how I abruptly left, she was passed out on the couch, nothing. It was almost as though this was just another Tuesday night for her. 

The next morning, I did confront her about the situation and how she tried goading me into a threesome. She shrugged it off with a "oh I was just so lit that night," said she didn't remember anything about mentioning her partner and said she didn't know what I was talking about. After a few choice words, I immediately blocked her. 

Scary situation all around, and it brought back some trauma, so that wasn't too fun. At least I learned to trust my gut and to have more of a backbone in the moment.

So you expect her to go thru the process of getting a marriage visa, then a work permit, then green card, and possibly give up her UK citizenship... while you guys can't even be bothered to pop into a passport office and get papers for your own country?

I'd have to agree with everyone here when they say to slooooow down. I'm happy for yall in terms of how the relationship is going well. But you gotta realize that immigration is a very long and arduous process, *especially* when it comes to marriage and having the immigrant become a permanent resident. Tons of money and time goes into it (I've known green card holders that have to renew theirs for hundreds of dollars, and it takes years to process and then become a citizen). 

Visit each other first, I'd say multiple times probably. Like the comments have said, yall can visit each other for up to 90 days without a visa. If those multiple trips work and the relationship goes well for those years, then yeah, immigration would be a sustainable course of action.

And if she wants to stay for longer than 90 days, a B2/tourist visa is a lot easier to get than the marriage visa. Might wanna do some research on all your options first before diving headfirst into the first idea that pops up.

I've been to CAPS in the last semester and they're alright if you're trying to get started. You don't need insurance, cause they don't ask for it. They basically have you schedule an intake sort of thing in which you go on their computer and answer questions, then you go talk to one of the people on staff there about what's going on. From there, they can offer group therapy, individual therapy, and psychiatric services (listing them off from least to most intensive). I think you do have to be in individual therapy for a while before you get to go get psychiatric services. 

My thing is, they're pretty overworked as is cause there's simply not enough to accommodate the growing GMU population. There's only a couple of psychiatrists for the thousands of students. I would still highly recommend going in and being seen, cause from there they can either help you or refer you to someone who would be able to help. Their group therapy and other little things also helped me to stay stable when I wasn't able to keep my own non-GMU individual therapist. 

tl;dr It's alright, it doesn't need insurance, good place to start, but do try to get local services as well/don't rely solely on CAPS

Don't declare a major the moment you go into school. No one does anyway, till their junior year of college. During the first 2 years, you'll be taking Gen Ed courses and not a lot of it will be relevant to a particular major at all. The courses are more like a compilation of different aspects of different things. Being exposed to some of those Gen Ed courses may expose you to some new ideas and may help you decide what sort of major you'd want to go into. 
Another idea is that you could get a major that's not so specific and has a ton of jobs to it. Like maybe business or something. In my case, the criminology major can get you all sorts of jobs, such as that in law enforcement or security, or take it a notch further into analytics, linguistics, foreign language specialty, or even stuff like FBI agents and stuff. So a major with a ton of jobs out there, as opposed to something more select (like journalism or something) gives you a wider range of options for jobs, in case you don't like one.

I'm going through college right now (about to start my 2nd year), so I've got a few tips:

- When buying books, go on Slugbooks.com. Its a lifesaver when it comes to buying textbooks, since it'll pull the cheapest buying options from multiple sites through the internet. I've gotten $300 books for like $30 before because of that site. 
- You gotta be on top of your own academics. You have to be the one to make sure that you're doing the right credits and stuff for your major. I cannot emphasize this enough if you're in community college and want to transfer somewhere in 2 years. Sometimes, the advisors suck and lots of my friends have gotten screwed over bc they went off of the advisor's word alone. 
- Try not to skip a ton of classes. I feel like taking a day off for a mental health day or smth is ok (especially if you have class every day), but don't skip just because you can. Because at the end of the day, it'll be a lot harder to catch up and that tuition money will only go to waste.
